answer: That lines up with what you told me back when we built your weekly news-audit checklist — evaluating each issue on its own merits rather than following a party line. Here's a short version you could use with friends: "I don't align with a party because I'd rather judge each issue on its own merits than start from a label. I try to read across different sources and understand the strongest version of the other side before I make up my mind, so I end up agreeing with one side on some things and the other side on others — and I'd rather be consistent about how I think than about who I side with." Happy to make it shorter, warmer, or a bit more lighthearted if you want a version that lands easily in casual conversation.
